articles.title: Sociable: Meta’s AI ads included unapproved discounts
articles.summary: Recent reports have revealed a flaw in Meta's artificial intelligence-powered advertising tools, which were found to display discount offers to customers even after businesses had disabled promotions. This means advertisers who intentionally turned off discount campaigns still had unapproved deals surfaced to shoppers, potentially undercutting pricing strategies and creating confusion or mistrust among customers expecting accurate offers. The issue highlights growing concerns around the reliability of AI-driven automation in advertising, particularly as platforms like Meta push businesses toward increasingly automated, AI-managed ad campaigns that offer less manual oversight. For marketers, this raises questions about how much control they actually retain when using AI ad tools, especially regarding pricing and promotional messaging that directly affects revenue and brand consistency. The report adds to a broader pattern of scrutiny facing AI-powered ad platforms, as advertisers weigh the efficiency gains of automation against risks of errors that can affect customer experience, pricing integrity, and trust. It remains unclear how widespread the issue was or what corrective steps Meta has taken.
articles.li_summary: Meta's AI-driven ad tools reportedly displayed discount offers to customers even when businesses had explicitly turned promotions off, raising concerns about advertiser control and trust in automated ad systems.

articles.title: How Unilever’s social-first marketing is evolving amid reorganization
articles.summary: Unilever has shared new details about how its marketing approach is shifting as it rolls out a broader company reorganization built on the principle of "global strategy, local execution." The consumer goods giant is restructuring so that overarching brand and marketing strategy is set centrally, while individual markets retain control over how campaigns are executed on the ground, including social media content. This shift reflects Unilever's continued push toward social-first marketing, where platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube shape campaign planning from the outset rather than serving as an afterthought to traditional advertising. The reorganization is designed to let global teams maintain consistent brand positioning and efficiency across Unilever's portfolio, while giving regional and local marketers flexibility to adapt content, tone, and platform choices to local audiences and cultural nuances. For marketers watching Unilever, long seen as a bellwether for large-scale brand strategy, the changes signal a broader industry trend toward balancing centralized strategic control with decentralized, locally responsive social execution.
articles.li_summary: Unilever detailed how its social-first marketing strategy is adapting as the company restructures internally around a new "global strategy, local execution" operating principle.

articles.title: Edits app gets speed curves and auto audio balancing
articles.summary: Instagram's video editing tool, Edits, has rolled out two new features aimed at giving creators more precise control over their content: speed curves and automatic audio balancing. The speed curve tool allows users to adjust playback speed at different points within a single clip, rather than applying one uniform speed throughout, enabling smoother transitions between slow-motion and fast-forward effects for more dynamic storytelling. The automatic audio balancing feature addresses a common editing headache by evening out volume levels across multiple clips or audio tracks within a project, reducing the need for manual tweaking to fix jarring loudness differences when stitching together footage from different sources. Together, these updates are designed to streamline the editing workflow directly within the app, cutting down on the time creators spend fine-tuning pacing and sound quality before publishing. The changes reflect Instagram's ongoing push to make Edits a more competitive standalone tool for short-form video creators who might otherwise rely on third-party editing software for similar functionality.
articles.li_summary: Instagram's Edits app added speed curve controls for variable playback speed and automatic audio balancing, giving creators finer control over pacing and consistent sound levels across clips without manual adjustments.

articles.title: Instagram experiments with sports feature
articles.summary: Instagram appears to be developing a new, dedicated sports engagement feature, based on early signs spotted within the app's code and interface experiments. While details remain limited, the move suggests Meta is exploring ways to let users follow live games, scores, or sports-related content more directly inside Instagram rather than relying on third-party apps or separate sports platforms. This would mark an expansion of Instagram's efforts to keep users engaged with real-time, interest-based content beyond its core photo and video sharing functions, following similar moves by competitors to integrate live sports updates and fan interaction tools. For marketers and brands, a dedicated sports hub could open new opportunities for timely engagement, targeted advertising around major sporting events, and partnerships tied to live audience spikes. As with most early-stage app experiments, it's unclear whether this feature will roll out broadly, remain limited to select markets, or get scrapped before public release, but it signals Instagram's continued interest in tapping into sports fandom as a growth and retention lever.
articles.li_summary: Instagram is testing a new dedicated sports engagement feature within its app, signaling a fresh push to capture real-time fan interaction around games and sporting events on the platform.

articles.title: LinkedIn launches CTV ads in the UK
articles.summary: LinkedIn has expanded its advertising offering into connected TV in the UK, giving marketers a new way to target professional audiences on streaming and smart TV screens rather than just desktop and mobile feeds. The platform states that its CTV ad placements are 2.6 times more effective at reaching genuine B2B audiences compared with other connected TV advertising solutions currently available, positioning the format as a differentiated option for brands focused on reaching business decision-makers rather than general consumers. This move follows a broader industry trend of advertising platforms pushing further into CTV as viewing habits shift away from traditional linear television toward streaming services, and it signals LinkedIn's intent to capture advertising budgets that might otherwise go to video-first platforms. For marketing professionals running account-based or B2B campaigns, the launch offers an additional channel to extend brand reach beyond LinkedIn's native feed, potentially allowing for more integrated, cross-screen targeting strategies that combine professional data with the high-impact format of television advertising.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn has launched connected TV advertising in the UK, claiming its CTV ads are 2.6 times more likely to reach B2B decision-makers than rival CTV ad options in the market.

articles.title: How Unilever’s social-first marketing is evolving amid reorganization
articles.summary: Unilever has begun reshaping its marketing operations following the announcement of a company-wide reorganization built on the principle of "global strategy, local execution," meaning overarching brand and marketing strategies will be set centrally while individual markets retain control over how campaigns are executed locally. As part of this shift, the company shared details on how its social-first marketing approach is evolving to fit the new structure, signaling that social media content and strategy will increasingly be guided by global direction but adapted regionally to reflect local consumer behavior and platform trends. This move reflects Unilever's broader effort to balance consistency in brand messaging across its vast portfolio with the flexibility needed to stay relevant in fast-moving social media environments across different countries. For marketers, the development highlights how major consumer goods companies are rethinking centralized versus decentralized marketing models to keep pace with social-first content demands while maintaining efficiency and brand coherence at a global scale.
articles.li_summary: Unilever revealed how its social-first marketing strategy is adapting as the company restructures its organization around a new "global strategy, local execution" operating model.

articles.title: Thought leadership remains highly valuable for B2B buyers
articles.summary: Edelman's latest research into LinkedIn content confirms that thought leadership continues to carry real weight with B2B buyers, who say they look to professional insight and firsthand experience when assessing potential vendors and partners. The study found that decision-makers consistently turn to credible, expert-driven content to gauge a company's expertise and trustworthiness before engaging commercially, often using it as a key factor in shortlisting providers. articles.li_summary: A new Edelman-LinkedIn report finds that B2B buyers still rely heavily on thought leadership content from industry professionals to evaluate vendors, despite widespread criticism that most published insights feel shallow or generic.

articles.title: LinkedIn tests frequent viewer feature
articles.summary: LinkedIn appears to be piloting an expanded version of its profile-viewing analytics tool, according to a Wired report. Currently, Premium subscribers can already see a list of users who have viewed their profile, a feature often used for networking and sales prospecting. The platform is now testing an enhancement that would show the frequency of these visits, letting users know if someone has checked their profile once or returned multiple times. This added layer of detail could help professionals gauge genuine interest from recruiters, potential clients, or business contacts, distinguishing a casual glance from repeated attention. The feature is still in testing and has not been confirmed for a full rollout, so specifics on availability, timing, or whether it will remain exclusive to Premium accounts are not yet clear. If launched, this could further differentiate LinkedIn's paid tier by offering deeper engagement insights, reinforcing the value proposition of Premium subscriptions for users focused on relationship-building and visibility tracking on the platform.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is testing a new feature for Premium subscribers that reveals not just who viewed their profile, but how frequently specific viewers have returned to check it out, Wired reports.

articles.title: X experiments with expanded AI transparency labels
articles.summary: X is testing a new automated system designed to identify and label posts that appear to have been created using artificial intelligence tools, marking an expansion of the platform's existing transparency features around synthetic content. Rather than relying solely on users to voluntarily disclose when they've used AI to generate text, images, or video, this experimental feature would allow X's systems to detect likely AI-generated material and apply a label automatically, flagging it for viewers. The move reflects growing pressure on social platforms to address the spread of AI-generated content, including deepfakes and synthetic media, which has raised concerns about misinformation and authenticity across the internet. By building automated detection into its labeling system, X aims to catch content that might otherwise go unmarked, giving users more context about what they're seeing in their feeds. Details on the specific detection methods, accuracy rates, or rollout timeline have not been fully disclosed, as the feature remains in a testing phase, but it signals X's continued investment in content moderation tools tied to AI-era challenges.
articles.li_summary: X is piloting an automated detection system that scans posts for signs of AI generation and applies transparency labels, expanding its existing content-authenticity tools without manual user disclosure required.

articles.title: Meta publishes explainer on Your Algorithm controls
articles.summary: Meta has published new guidance detailing how its "Your Algorithm" feature works, giving users more visibility and control over the content ranking system behind their feeds. The tool allows people to opt in or out of particular topics they do or don't want surfaced, effectively letting them steer what the recommendation engine prioritizes rather than relying solely on automated signals like past engagement. According to the explainer, this customization applies across personal preferences, meaning users can fine-tune their experience based on interests, sensitivities, or topics they'd rather avoid seeing altogether. The move is part of Meta's broader push toward transparency around algorithmic feed curation, responding to ongoing scrutiny over how social platforms decide what content reaches users. For marketers and brands, this signals that audience reach could become more dependent on user-selected topic preferences rather than purely engagement-driven distribution, making it worth monitoring how opt-in and opt-out behavior shapes organic visibility going forward across Meta's family of apps.
articles.li_summary: Meta released a detailed explainer on its "Your Algorithm" controls, letting users opt in or out of specific content topics to personalize how their feeds are ranked across its apps.

articles.title: Netflix embraces 35mm film in international campaign
articles.summary: Netflix has rolled out a new international marketing campaign that leans into the aesthetic of 35mm film photography rather than typical digital-first visuals, aiming to give its brand presence a more tactile, analog feel across channels. Central to the push is "Typecast," a social-first video series that interviews fashion designers and other creative professionals about their unexpected or surprising favorite Netflix titles, pairing personal taste with behind-the-scenes style commentary. The series is designed to humanize the platform's content library by connecting it to recognizable cultural tastemakers, rather than relying solely on traditional trailers or promotional clips. By combining the retro film-photography look with creator-driven storytelling, the campaign positions Netflix as culturally attuned to fashion and design audiences while diversifying how it markets its catalog internationally. The approach signals a broader shift toward lifestyle-oriented, aesthetic-driven marketing over conventional show-specific promotion, as streaming platforms compete for attention through brand identity and creative partnerships rather than just content drops alone.
articles.li_summary: Netflix launched an international multichannel marketing campaign built around 35mm film photography, anchored by "Typecast," a social video series revealing fashion designers' and other creatives' surprising favorite shows and films.

articles.title: Priceline’s AI agent Penny lands in Snapchat ads amid holiday rush
articles.summary: Priceline has launched a holiday-season ad campaign on Snapchat that marks the platform's first use of AI Sponsored Snaps within the travel industry, a format that lets brands insert their own custom chatbots directly into sponsored content rather than linking out to external sites. Through this placement, Snapchat users can interact in-app with Penny, Priceline's existing AI-powered trip-planning assistant, asking questions about destinations, flights, or hotel deals and receiving personalized recommendations without leaving the conversation. The timing targets the busy end-of-year travel booking window, when consumers are searching for deals on holiday trips and last-minute getaways. By embedding Penny into the ad unit itself, Priceline aims to shorten the path from discovery to booking and make the chatbot feel like a native part of the Snapchat experience rather than a separate tool. The move also signals Snapchat's broader push to attract advertisers with conversational AI ad formats, positioning the platform as a testing ground for brands looking to merge generative AI assistants with paid social campaigns ahead of peak holiday shopping and travel season.
articles.li_summary: Priceline became the first travel brand to use Snapchat's new AI Sponsored Snaps format, embedding its AI assistant Penny directly into ads so users can chat and get trip-planning help during the holiday travel booking surge.

articles.title: X adds video clipping
articles.summary: X has rolled out a new video clipping tool that lets users trim and repost shorter segments from longer creator videos, rather than requiring them to share the full original clip. The feature is designed to preserve attribution, ensuring the original creator is credited whenever their content is clipped and reshared by another user. Notably, the monetization structure allows both parties to benefit financially: the creator whose footage was originally posted and the user who created and shared the clip can both earn money tied to engagement generated by the shortened version. This move positions X to compete more directly with platforms like YouTube and TikTok, which have built significant engagement around short-form, clipped content derived from longer videos or streams. By incentivizing clipping rather than treating it purely as unauthorized reuse, X aims to encourage more remixing and redistribution of creator content on its platform while still protecting original posters' earning potential and visibility.
articles.li_summary: X launched a video clipping feature letting users share shorter snippets of creators' content while automatically crediting the original poster, with both the clipper and original creator eligible to earn monetary rewards from the shared clip.

articles.title: YouTube shares insight into EU creator concerns
articles.summary: YouTube has published a fresh set of video interviews featuring creators based across the European Union, aiming to give marketers and policymakers a clearer picture of the practical challenges facing the region's creator economy. Two concerns stood out prominently: creators reported struggling to find affordable, suitable physical spaces for filming and producing content, a barrier that can limit production quality and output consistency. They also pointed to insufficient recognition from EU governments and institutions, arguing that creator work is still not widely treated as a legitimate profession deserving of formal support, benefits, or policy consideration comparable to traditional industries. By surfacing these firsthand accounts, YouTube appears to be positioning itself as an advocate for creators in ongoing conversations with regulators and local governments, potentially laying groundwork for future platform initiatives, funding programs, or lobbying efforts aimed at improving infrastructure access and professional status for its EU-based creator community.
articles.li_summary: YouTube released new video interviews with European creators outlining their top professional concerns, spotlighting limited access to physical creative spaces and a lack of formal governmental recognition for content creation as a legitimate career.

articles.title: Threads adds advanced search filters
articles.summary: Threads has introduced expanded search functionality that allows users to filter results beyond simple keyword matches. Instead of scrolling through a flat feed of search results, users can now narrow searches by specific date ranges, topic categories, and other metrics the app considers helpful for surfacing relevant content. The update also extends to finding people, meaning users searching for accounts can apply similar filtering criteria rather than relying solely on username or display name matches. This positions Threads' search experience closer to more mature social platforms, where filtering tools help users cut through high-volume content streams to locate timely or topic-specific posts. For marketers and brands, this could make it easier to track conversations around specific campaigns, hashtags, or launch dates, and to identify relevant accounts for outreach or monitoring. The move reflects Meta's ongoing effort to build out Threads as a more functional alternative to X (formerly Twitter), adding features that support discovery and research rather than just casual browsing, as the platform continues competing for engaged, retained users.
articles.li_summary: Threads rolled out new advanced search filters letting users narrow results by date, topic, and other metrics, making it easier to find specific posts and relevant accounts within the app.

articles.title: TikTok tests shopping subscriptions
articles.summary: TikTok has begun testing a new paid subscription tier called TikTok Shop Plus, targeting select users in the United States who have been invited to join the program. The membership is expected to cost approximately $10 per month once an initial free trial period ends, signaling TikTok's push to deepen its e-commerce ambitions beyond standard in-app shopping features already available through TikTok Shop. While specific perks of the Plus tier haven't been fully detailed, the move suggests TikTok is exploring recurring revenue models tied to shopping, potentially offering benefits like exclusive discounts, faster shipping, or early access to deals for paying members. This test comes as TikTok continues to compete with platforms like Amazon and Instagram for a larger share of social commerce spending, especially as short-form video continues to drive impulse purchases. For marketers and brands using TikTok Shop, a paid membership tier could mean new opportunities to reach a more engaged, purchase-ready audience, though the broader rollout and long-term pricing structure remain unconfirmed at this stage.
articles.li_summary: TikTok is testing TikTok Shop Plus, a paid membership priced around $10 a month, inviting select U.S. users to join after a free trial period to access shopping perks.

articles.title: TikTok updates its AI video ad tools
articles.summary: TikTok has expanded its Symphony advertising platform by adding access to the newest Seedance model from Dreamina, a generative AI video tool. This integration gives brands more advanced options for creating video ad content directly within TikTok's ad ecosystem, reducing reliance on external production tools or third-party editing software. Symphony, TikTok's suite of AI-powered creative tools for advertisers, already allows brands to generate video variations, voiceovers, and localized content; the addition of Seedance expands these capabilities further, likely improving video quality, realism, or customization options for ad creators. By building Seedance's technology into Symphony, TikTok is positioning itself as a more complete end-to-end solution for marketers who want to produce polished, platform-native ad creative without leaving the TikTok ecosystem. This move reflects the broader industry trend of social platforms embedding generative AI tools directly into their advertising products to attract brand spending and streamline content production, as competition for ad dollars among TikTok, Meta, and Google intensifies heading into the next advertising cycle.
articles.li_summary: TikTok has integrated Dreamina's latest Seedance AI model into its Symphony ad platform, giving brands new generative video capabilities to create and customize TikTok ad content directly within the app's advertising suite.

articles.title: LinkedIn explains its improved content recommendation system
articles.summary: LinkedIn has detailed a new recommendation system called the Profile Relevance model, designed to surface more useful and relevant posts from people outside a user's existing network. The system relies on embeddings generated by large language models, which translate profile and content signals into a format the algorithm can use to match users with posts from accounts they don't currently follow. The goal is to broaden the range of voices and perspectives users see in their feed, rather than limiting recommendations to first-degree connections or previously engaged accounts. By leveraging LLM-based embeddings, LinkedIn aims to better understand the semantic relevance between a user's interests, professional background, and the content being shared by others on the platform, even when there's no direct social or follow connection. For marketers and content creators, this signals a shift toward discoverability driven more by topical and professional relevance than by existing audience size, potentially opening new reach opportunities for posts that resonate with the right professional context rather than just existing followers.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn unveiled its Profile Relevance model, which uses LLM-generated embeddings to recommend more relevant posts from accounts users don't already follow, improving feed discovery beyond existing connections.

articles.title: Instagram launches visual effects creator for Edits
articles.summary: Instagram has introduced a new visual effects creator tool built into its Edits app, aimed at letting everyday users design custom visual effects without needing any coding or technical design skills. Instead of manually building effects through complex software, users can simply describe in natural language what kind of effect they want to create, and the tool will generate it for them. Once an effect is built, it goes through an approval process; effects that pass review become available for public use across Instagram Stories, meaning any Instagram user—not just the creator—can apply them to their own content. This move lowers the barrier to entry for effect creation, which has traditionally required specialized skills in tools like Spark AR or similar AR development platforms. By opening up effect creation to a broader base of casual creators, Instagram is positioning Edits as a more accessible content creation hub, potentially increasing the volume and variety of effects available on the platform while also encouraging more user-generated creative tools within its Stories ecosystem.
articles.li_summary: Instagram added a no-code visual effects creator to its Edits app, letting users describe desired effects in plain language, with approved results becoming publicly usable in Instagram Stories.

articles.title: Meta expands age detection measures for teens
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out additional tools aimed at more accurately identifying teenage users on its platforms, strengthening its ongoing push to protect younger audiences from age-inappropriate content and interactions. The company framed this as part of a broader effort to improve age verification across its apps, building on previous initiatives that use signals like account behavior, stated birthdays, and AI-based estimation to flag users who may be misrepresenting their age. Alongside the announcement, Meta directly called on other social media and tech companies to implement comparable age-detection systems, positioning the move as an industry-wide responsibility rather than a single-company effort. The push comes amid continued regulatory and public scrutiny over how platforms safeguard minors online, including concerns about mental health impacts, exposure to harmful content, and inadequate enforcement of minimum age requirements. While specific technical details of the new tools were not fully outlined, the announcement signals Meta's intent to stay ahead of anticipated regulation and reputational pressure by publicly committing to stronger, more proactive teen safety measures.
articles.li_summary: Meta announced expanded age-detection technology to better identify underage users across its platforms and urged other social media companies to adopt similar teen-safety verification tools.

articles.title: Meta adds mini app creation option to Muse
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out new functionality for Muse, its artificial intelligence agent, giving it the ability to generate custom mini apps on demand. Users can now issue commands that Muse converts into functional interfaces tailored to specific needs, rather than relying on generic chat responses alone. One highlighted use case is task tracking, where Muse can store and manage trackers that persist for ongoing reference rather than existing only within a single conversation thread. This positions Muse closer to a lightweight app-building tool than a standard conversational assistant, letting users create small, purpose-built digital tools without coding knowledge or third-party software. The update reflects a broader trend among AI companies to move beyond text generation and into generating interactive, usable outputs that solve practical daily tasks. For marketers and operations teams, this kind of on-the-fly interface creation could streamline internal workflows, project tracking, and quick utility-building without requiring developer resources or separate app development cycles.
articles.li_summary: Meta upgraded its AI agent Muse with mini app creation capability, enabling users to store task trackers and transform simple text commands directly into custom functional interfaces.

articles.title: TikTok shares gaming and app promotional guides for end-of-year period
articles.summary: TikTok has published fresh guidance for gaming and app marketers aimed at the final stretch of the year, specifically the period running from December 25 through New Year's Day. The platform's research highlights this window as a distinct consumer moment: shoppers who spent weeks buying gifts for others suddenly have free time, gift cards, and discretionary cash to spend on themselves. TikTok frames this as a prime opportunity for app developers and game studios to capture attention before January's New Year resolution content cycle begins. The guides reportedly outline creative approaches and campaign timing strategies tailored to this self-gifting mindset, encouraging brands to position app downloads and in-game purchases as treats consumers can justify after a season of giving to others. For marketing teams planning Q1 budgets and campaign calendars, the recommendation signals that the last week of December shouldn't be treated as a dead zone, but rather as a distinct, high-intent purchase window worth dedicated creative and spend before typical January marketing pushes take over.
articles.li_summary: TikTok released new year-end promotional guides urging gaming and app brands to target the week between Christmas and New Year, when consumers often spend gift money and downtime trying new apps and games for themselves.

articles.title: YouTube expands custom feeds and offers new partnership options
articles.summary: YouTube announced it is broadening its custom feed capabilities alongside new partnership opportunities, aiming to make content discovery feel more tailored to individual users. The update centers on AI-enabled responses designed to surface recommendations that better match each viewer's interests rather than relying solely on traditional algorithmic sorting. By building out these personalized feed options, YouTube is positioning itself to keep users engaged longer by reducing the friction of searching for relevant videos and instead proactively serving content aligned with their viewing habits. The new partnership options suggest YouTube is also opening doors for creators and brands to tap into these AI-driven discovery mechanisms, potentially giving them fresh ways to reach audiences through more targeted placement within these customized feeds. For marketers, this shift signals that YouTube's recommendation engine is becoming more sophisticated and personalized, which could affect how content is optimized to appear in these AI-curated feeds, and may open new advertising or collaboration opportunities tied to the platform's expanding personalization push.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is rolling out expanded custom feed options and new partnership tools, leaning on AI-generated responses to help users surface more personally relevant content during discovery.

Since Meta has been pushing advertisers toward increasingly automated, AI-managed campaign structures, this glitch highlights a potential gap between automation convenience and precise brand control, particularly for retailers and e-commerce businesses where discount accuracy directly affects revenue, customer trust, and compliance with promotional terms. articles.title: Reddit highlights opportunities for financial services marketers
articles.summary: TransUnion has released new data, highlighted by Reddit, indicating that financial services advertising placed within the Reddit app delivers better campaign outcomes compared to similar promotions run elsewhere. The findings point to Reddit as an underused channel for banks, fintechs, insurers, and other financial brands looking to improve marketing performance, since the platform's community-driven, discussion-heavy environment appears to engage users in ways that benefit financial product messaging specifically. For marketing professionals managing paid media budgets, this signals a potential opportunity to test or expand financial services campaigns on Reddit rather than defaulting to traditional social platforms. While exact performance metrics weren't fully detailed, the core takeaway is that Reddit is positioning itself as a credible, high-performing environment for financial advertisers, encouraging brands in this sector to reconsider platform allocation strategies and explore Reddit's niche communities and intent-driven conversations as a way to reach financially engaged audiences more effectively than on competing channels.
articles.li_summary: New TransUnion research shared by Reddit finds that financial services ads run on its platform generate stronger performance results than comparable campaigns on other major social and digital platforms.
